title: Burden of novel and ultra-rare missense variants in the NF-kappaB pathway genes associated to Meniere's disease.
authors: Cruz-Granados, Pablo; Rivero de Jesus, Victoria; Soto-Varela, Andres; Gonzalez-Aguado, Rocio; Lopez-Escamez, Jose A
one_liner_zh: 该研究分析梅尼埃病中NF-kB通路基因的罕见变异，结合蛋白建模与受体-配体对接预测变异对蛋白-DNA/蛋白互作界面的影响，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作建模但非TF-DNA核心体系，方法可迁移。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Meniere's disease (MD) is an inner ear disorder characterised by tinnitus, sensorineural hearing loss and dizziness, although around 60% of patients also exhibit and immune dysregulation. Transcriptomic studies have identified three distinct immune phenotypes in MD, classified based on systemic inflammation, cytokine profiles and association to autoinflammatory/autoimmune comorbidities. Furthermore, genetic studies have shown aggregation of rare variants in MD patients; however, the relationship between genetic factors and immune responses remains poorly understood. METHODS: In this study, we analysed exome data pertaining to NF-kappaB pathway genes to identify ultrarare variants that could contribute to the immune phenotypes observed in MD. Furthermore, we retrieved MD epigenetic and transcriptomic data to search for the associated molecular signature. We performed protein modelling and receptor-ligand docking, as well as differential transcript usage (DTU) and splicing prediction. RESULTS: We identified ultrarare heterozygous variants in TLR9 (chr3:52222299 G>C and chr3:52223761 C>A), TNFRSF1B (chr1:12167150 C>T and chr1:12202100 G>A), and FAS (chr10:89003139 G>A and chr10:89008919 C>T) in MD patients. Splicing predictions suggested potential creation of cryptic donor/acceptor sites for TLR9 and TNFRSF1B variants. Protein modelling predicted destabilising effects for all three proteins, with altered atomic interactions in TNFRSF1B and FAS. When docked, the TLR9-TLR9 dimer and FAS-FASGL models, redistributed interfacial contacts, potentially reducing binding efficiency, whereas docked TNFRSF1B-TRAF2 interactions were partially maintained. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that MD distinct immune phenotypes based on systemic inflammation and may be linked to comorbid autoimmune/autoinflammatory disorders, with rare variants in TLR9, TNFRSF1B and FAS likely contributing to autoinflammation.
abstract_zh: 引言：梅尼埃病（Meniere's disease, MD）是一种内耳疾病，特征为耳鸣、感音神经性听力损失和眩晕，尽管约60%的患者还表现出免疫失调。转录组学研究已根据全身炎症、细胞因子谱及与自身炎症/自身免疫共病的关联，在MD中识别出三种不同的免疫表型。此外，遗传学研究显示MD患者中罕见变异存在聚集；然而，遗传因素与免疫反应之间的关系仍知之甚少。方法：在本研究中，我们分析了与NF-kappaB通路基因相关的外显子组数据，以识别可能促成MD中观察到的免疫表型的超罕见变异。此外，我们检索了MD的表观遗传学和转录组学数据，以寻找相关的分子特征。我们进行了蛋白质建模和受体-配体对接，以及差异转录使用（differential transcript usage, DTU）和剪接预测。结果：我们在MD患者中识别出TLR9（chr3:52222299 G>C和chr3:52223761 C>A）、TNFRSF1B（chr1:12167150 C>T和chr1:12202100 G>A）和FAS（chr10:89003139 G>A和chr10:89008919 C>T）中的超罕见杂合变异。剪接预测提示TLR9和TNFRSF1B变异可能产生隐蔽供体/受体位点。蛋白质建模预测所有三种蛋白质均具有去稳定效应，其中TNFRSF1B和FAS的原子相互作用发生改变。对接时，TLR9-TLR9二聚体和FAS-FASGL模型重新分布了界面接触，可能降低结合效率，而对接的TNFRSF1B-TRAF2相互作用部分维持。结论：这些发现表明，MD基于全身炎症的独特免疫表型可能与共病自身免疫/自身炎症疾病相关，TLR9、TNFRSF1B和FAS中的罕见变异可能促成自身炎症。
